text: 123451 of 7Introduction to Electric MotorsThis lesson explains the basic steps of how an electric motor works, turning electrical energy into mechanical motion.START2 of 7Step 1Current Enters the CoilElectric current flows into a coil of wire inside the motor. This is like plugging in a fan or turning on a toy car.3 of 7Step 2Magnetic Field Exerts ForceThe coil sits in a magnetic field, often created by permanent magnets or electromagnets. The current in the coil interacts with the magnetic field, producing a force on the wire.4 of 7Step 3Coil Begins to RotateThis force causes the coil to turn. Imagine pushing a swing—each push keeps it moving. In a motor, the force keeps the coil spinning.5 of 7Step 4Commutator Reverses CurrentAs the coil turns, a commutator switches the direction of the current at just the right moment. This ensures the rotation continues smoothly in the same direction.6 of 7Step 5Mechanical Work ProducedThe spinning coil can now do useful work, like turning wheels or spinning blades. The motor has successfully turned electrical energy into motion.7 of 7Summary: How Electric Motors WorkIn summary, an electric motor takes in electrical energy and, through the interaction of current and magnetic fields, produces mechanical motion that powers countless devices.START AGAIN

123451 of 7Introduction to How a Generator Produces ElectricityThis lesson explains the process by which a generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy, step by step.START2 of 7Step 1Coil Begins to RotateMechanical energy, such as a spinning wind turbine or turning handle, rotates a coil of wire inside the generator.3 of 7Step 2Magnetic Flux ChangesAs the coil spins in a magnetic field, the amount of magnetic field passing through the coil (magnetic flux) changes continuously.4 of 7Step 3Voltage is InducedThis changing magnetic flux induces a voltage across the ends of the coil, following Faraday’s Law of electromagnetic induction.5 of 7Step 4Current is ProducedThe induced voltage causes an electric current to flow through the circuit connected to the generator.6 of 7Step 5Electrical Energy OutputThe generator delivers electrical energy, which can be used to power homes, devices, or entire cities.7 of 7Summary: Generator Energy ConversionIn summary, a generator transforms mechanical energy into electrical energy by rotating a coil in a magnetic field, creating a current that can be harnessed for countless applications.START AGAIN

12341 of 6Introduction to Dynamic MicrophonesDynamic microphones are widely used in audio recording and live sound. Let's explore how they convert sound waves into electrical signals.START2 of 6Step 1Sound Vibrates the DiaphragmWhen you speak or sing, sound waves hit the microphone's thin diaphragm, causing it to vibrate.3 of 6Step 2Coil Moves in Magnetic FieldThe diaphragm is attached to a small coil of wire, which moves back and forth inside a magnetic field as the diaphragm vibrates.4 of 6Step 3Voltage is InducedThe movement of the coil in the magnetic field changes the magnetic flux, inducing a voltage across the coil ends.5 of 6Step 4Electrical Signal ProducedThis induced voltage creates an electrical signal that matches the original sound wave, ready to be amplified or recorded.6 of 6Summary: How a Dynamic Microphone WorksIn summary, a dynamic microphone transforms sound energy into electrical energy using the same principles as a generator, allowing us to capture and transmit sound.START AGAIN
